note: What the host was doing while the GPU idled (no kernel, no copy in flight), by the CUDA/HIP runtime or driver API call in flight (an nsys export's CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_RUNTIME rows; a version suffix such as _v4000 is dropped before matching). Read only through collectors/time_budget.py. Each instant of a gap goes to the first row (in this file's order) whose call is in flight then; an instant with no call in flight is `cpu` (the host computing, or waiting on something that is not a GPU API call). The calls are every thread's of the traced processes (the export's rows carry no thread filter here): a blocking call on a helper thread counts for the gap it overlaps. ORDER MATTERS: a slow host-side call (register, allocate) comes before the waits it overlaps.

causes.copy_call: a copy call the host waits in
causes.sync: the host waiting for the GPU (synchronize)
causes.launch: launching work (kernel or graph launch calls)
causes.cpu_work: CPU work (no GPU API call in flight)
